sections.title: Appendix G: References
sections.summary: Bibliography of standards, manuals, and guide specifications cited throughout UFC 3-250-04, organized by publishing body: DoD Unified Facilities Criteria/Guide Specifications, Army engineer manuals/regulations and the extensive CRD-C concrete test-method/specification series, American Concrete Institute publications, ASTM International standards, and single citations from IPRF, NRMCA, and PCA.
sections.body:
Appendix G is an unnumbered bibliography, organized by publishing body rather than by numbered subheading, listing every standard, manual, and guide specification cited or incorporated by reference elsewhere in UFC 3-250-04.

It opens with Unified Facilities Criteria (UFC) citations, linked to the WBDG UFC portal: UFC 1-200-01 (DoD Building Code), UFC 3-250-01 (Pavement Design for Roads and Parking Areas), UFC 3-250-08 (Standard Practice for Sealing Joints and Cracks in Rigid and Flexible Pavements), UFC 3-250-11 (Soil Stabilization and Modification for Pavements), and UFC 3-260-02 (Pavement Design for Airfields).

Next is a Unified Facilities Guide Specifications (UFGS) block with a single Joint Service citation, TSPWG M 3-250-04.97.05 (Proportioning Concrete Mixtures with Graded Aggregates for Rigid Airfield Pavements), followed by an ARMY subsection listing EM 1110-2-2006 (Roller-Compacted Concrete) and ER 1110-34-1 (Transportation Systems Mandatory Center of Expertise).

The largest block is the Army's CRD-C standards series (Corps of Engineers concrete test methods and specifications, each explicitly cross-referenced in parentheses to its ASTM equivalent where one exists), spanning roughly CRD-C 3 through CRD-C 662. This series covers fresh-concrete properties (temperature, slump, unit weight/yield/air content by gravimetric, volumetric, and pressure methods, within-batch uniformity); specimen fabrication and curing, including the two RCC-specific standards CRD-C 160 (making RCC cylinder specimens on a vibrating table) and CRD-C 161 (selecting proportions for RCC using a vibrating table); hardened-concrete strength and durability testing (flexural strength, splitting tensile strength, resistance to rapid freezing and thawing, air-void-system petrography); aggregate testing (surface moisture, total evaporable moisture, petrographic examination, scratch hardness, aggregate specification limits per CRD-C 133/ASTM C33); admixture and cementitious-material specifications (air-entraining and chemical admixtures, blended hydraulic cements, performance hydraulic cements, ground-granulated blast-furnace slag, coal fly ash and natural pozzolan); curing-compound specifications and water-retention test methods; alkali-silica reactivity test methods (mortar-bar and length-change methods, plus a lithium-nitrate-admixture accelerated mortar-bar method); vibrator frequency/amplitude testing; and sulfate-ion determination in soil and water.

This is followed by American Concrete Institute (ACI) references -- ACI 207.5 (Roller Compacted Mass Concrete), ACI 211.3 (Standard Practice for Selecting Proportions for No-Slump Concrete), ACI 305 (Hot Weather Concreting), and ACI 306 (Cold Weather Concreting) -- then an extensive American Society for Testing and Materials (ASTM) list spanning roughly ASTM C31 through ASTM D6938, plus ASTM E177 and E965. The C-series parallels the CRD-C list's fresh/hardened concrete, aggregate, admixture, cement, and curing-compound topics (each CRD-C entry cites its ASTM counterpart directly). The D-series and E-series cover soil-cement moisture-density relationships (ASTM D558, D698, D1557), soil classification for engineering purposes (ASTM D2487), nuclear in-place density and water content of soil/soil-aggregate (ASTM D6938), and general testing-practice/precision-and-bias standards (ASTM E177, E965 pavement macrotexture depth).

The appendix closes with single citations to the Innovative Pavement Research Foundation (IPRF-01-G-002-1, Best Practices for Airport Portland Cement Concrete Construction), the National Ready Mixed Concrete Association (NRMCA certification of ready-mixed concrete production facilities), and the Portland Cement Association (PCA guide specifications for concrete subject to alkali-silica reactions).
key_points: Organized by publishing body, not by numbered subheading: UFC, UFGS (Joint Service and Army), Army CRD-C standards, ACI, ASTM, and single citations from IPRF, NRMCA, and PCA.
UFC citations include UFC 3-250-01 (road/parking pavement design), UFC 3-250-08 (joint/crack sealing), UFC 3-250-11 (soil stabilization for pavements), and UFC 3-260-02 (airfield pavement design).

Army references include EM 1110-2-2006 (Roller-Compacted Concrete) and the extensive CRD-C standard series (roughly CRD-C 3 to CRD-C 662), each cross-referenced to its ASTM equivalent where one exists.

CRD-C/ASTM standards cover fresh concrete properties, specimen fabrication/curing (including RCC-specific CRD-C 160/161), hardened-concrete strength and durability, aggregate testing, admixtures, cements (including blended/GGBFS/fly ash), curing compounds, and alkali-silica reactivity.
ACI references: ACI 207.5 (Roller Compacted Mass Concrete), ACI 211.3 (No-Slump Concrete Proportioning), ACI 305/306 (Hot/Cold Weather Concreting).
ASTM D-series references cover soil-cement moisture-density relationships (D558, D698, D1557), soil classification (D2487), and nuclear in-place density (D6938).
Non-standards-body citations: IPRF airport PCC construction best practices, NRMCA ready-mixed concrete facility certification, and PCA alkali-silica reaction guide specifications.
sections.applicability: Serves as the master bibliography of standards, manuals, and guide specifications referenced throughout UFC 3-250-04, including the RCC pavement provisions of Appendix E.
